# Brief: Simulado P2 (Processamento de Imagens), 6 pages

The document has 8 objective questions (QO1–QO8) and 2 discursive questions (QD1–QD2). It contains no answer key. Any "likely answer" below is my own working, not from the document.

Two things to know first. The text on p. 4 says the 6×6 image is for "questões objetivas 1, 2 e 3", but it is clearly meant for QO6–QO8. I read the figures on every page and describe them below.

## Shared text for QO1–QO2 (p. 1)
- A grayscale N×N image X is shown. It is the "Lena" photo with a hat. (p. 1)
- `X_dct = dct2(X)` is the DCT, described as a linear transform. Its absolute value is shown as a mostly black image with bright energy only in the top-left corner. (p. 1)
- Filtering is `Y = idct2(H.*X_dct);`. H is a binary 0/1 matrix, all zeros except an L×L square of ones at the top-left corner. (p. 1)

## QO1 (p. 2)
Statements: I. linear filtering. II. spatial filtering. III. high-pass filtering. Options: A) I; B) I e II; C) I e III; D) II e III; E) I, II e III.
- **Topics:** DCT and frequency-domain filtering, linearity, spatial versus frequency domain, low-pass versus high-pass.
- **Skill:** conceptual. You must recognise that keeping the top-left coefficients keeps low frequencies. My reading is that this is linear and low-pass, and it is frequency-domain, not spatial, so the answer is probably A.

## QO2 (p. 2)
Two images are shown. Y1 is sharp and only slightly blurred. Y2 is very blurred. Both come from different choices of L.
- I. The L for Y2 is smaller than the L for Y1.
- II. Z = X − Y2 consists predominantly of the edges of X.
- III. I = X + A*(X−Y1), with A a positive real number, is a version of X with enhanced edges.
Options: A) I; B) I e II; C) I e III; D) II e III; E) I, II e III.
- **Topics:** the effect of the cutoff size L, a residual (X minus low-pass) acting as a high-pass, and unsharp masking / high-boost.
- **Skill:** conceptual and visual. All three look true, so the answer is probably E.

## QO3 (pp. 2–3)
MATLAB function. The input is an RGB image X.
```
function Y = exemplo_funcao(X)
X = double(X)/255;
Y(:,:,1) = round(5*X(:,:,1))/5;
Y(:,:,2) = round(5*X(:,:,2))/5;
Y(:,:,3) = round(5*X(:,:,3))/5;
```
Statements: I. Y is X with reduced brightness. II. Y is X with changed hues. III. Y is the safe-colors representation of X. Options: A) I; B) II; C) III; D) II e III; E) I, II e III.
- **Topics:** RGB colour quantization, safe colors (6 levels per channel, 6³ = 216 colors), reading code.
- **Skill:** conceptual plus code interpretation. Each channel is quantized to {0, .2, .4, .6, .8, 1}. This probably gives II and III, so D. Watch the normalization: the output is in [0,1], not 0–255.

## QO4 (p. 3)
Three histograms of noisy images are shown. The x-axis runs 0–300.
- **Histogram 1:** spread over roughly 0–255 with no isolated spikes (y up to about 0.008).
- **Histogram 2:** a body spread from 0 to 255 plus a single tall spike at 255 (about 0.057).
- **Histogram 3:** a similar body with spikes at both 0 and 255 (about 0.055 each).

Question: which technique is appropriate for histograms 1, 2 and 3, respectively? Options:
- A) Filtro passa-baixa; filtro passa-alta e equalização de histograma.
- B) Equalização de histograma; correção gamma e filtro passa-alta.
- C) Filtro passa-faixa; filtro de média geométrica e filtro de média.
- D) Filtro de média; filtro de média contra-harmônica e filtro passa-alta.
- E) Filtro de média; filtro de média contra-harmônica e filtro de média alpha podada.

- **Topics:** noise models read from histograms (Gaussian/uniform, salt-only, salt-and-pepper) and restoration filters (mean, contra-harmonic, alpha-trimmed mean).
- **Skill:** conceptual and visual. Likely answer: E.

## QO5 (p. 4)
Image X is the grayscale Lena. Image Y is a binary black-and-white edge map of X, drawn as thin white contours. Which sequence produces Y from X? Options:
- A) i) passa-baixa; ii) limiarização; iii) passa-alta.
- B) i) passa-baixa; ii) passa-alta; iii) limiarização.
- C) i) limiarização; ii) passa-alta; iii) passa-baixa.
- D) i) passa-alta; ii) limiarização; iii) passa-baixa.
- E) i) limiarização; ii) passa-baixa; iii) passa-alta.

- **Topics:** edge detection pipeline (smoothing, then gradient/high-pass, then thresholding) and the ordering of operations.
- **Skill:** conceptual. Likely answer: B.

## Shared text for QO6–QO8 (p. 4)
This is a 6×6 RGB image with 8-bit integers, shown as (R,G,B). Rows are listed first, with columns 1–6 inside each row. (p. 4)
- **Row 1:** (123,107,243) (117,101,222) (115,100,199) (112,98,170) (112,102,133) (105,105,105)
- **Row 2:** (115,105,243) (112,99,213) (110,97,195) (109,96,163) (95,105,131) (98,103,115)
- **Row 3:** (112,104,241) (114,99,211) (43,97,44) (38,96,45) (51,108,45) (78,108,125)
- **Row 4:** (111,102,61) (111,100,78) (42,98,47) (0,95,0) (48,104,42) (49,104,129)
- **Row 5:** (109,101,33) (112,101,49) (44,99,39) (45,97,41) (44,103,55) (23,103,112)
- **Row 6:** (101,101,0) (111,102,37) (109,100,95) (104,98,152) (19,102,128) (0,102,102)

## QO6 (p. 4)
- I. The chromaticity of pixel (6,1) is cyan.
- II. Pixel (1,6) has minimum saturation.
- III. The brightness of pixel (5,2) is less than that of pixel (5,3).

Options: A) II; B) I e II; C) I e III; D) II e III; E) I, II e III.
- **Topics:** the HSI color model (hue, saturation, intensity) and the RGB-to-HSI relationship.
- **Skill:** small computations plus conceptual hue reasoning.
- **My check:**
  - (101,101,0) is yellow, so I is false.
  - (105,105,105) is gray, with S = 0, so II is true.
  - I(5,2) = 87.3 and I(5,3) = 60.7, so III is false.
  - Answer: A.

## QO7 (p. 5)
- I. The chromaticity of pixel (6,6) is yellow.
- II. Pixel (6,6) has maximum saturation.
- III. The brightness of pixel (2,2) equals that of pixel (3,2).

Options: A) I; B) I e II; C) I e III; D) II e III; E) I, II e III.
- **Topics:** the same HSI concepts as QO6.
- **My check:**
  - (0,102,102) is cyan, so I is false.
  - The minimum channel is 0, so S = 1 and II is true.
  - (112,99,213) and (114,99,211) both sum to 424, so the mean intensities are equal and III is true.
  - Answer: D.

## QO8 (p. 5)
Convert to safe colors (216 colors, uniformly distributed). What is the new (R,G,B) of X(3,3) = (43,97,44)? Options: A) (51,102,51); B) (101,109,102); C) (42,106,42); D) (128,85,213); E) (102,102,204).
- **Topics:** safe colors, with levels {0, 51, 102, 153, 204, 255}, and nearest-level quantization.
- **Skill:** a quick computation. 43→51, 97→102, 44→51, so the answer is A.

## QD1 (p. 5, discursive)
- Setup: a 3×3 grayscale image with L = 10 levels (0 = black, 9 = white).
- The matrix is X = [a b c; d e f; g h i].
- a…i are the digits of the student's matrícula (enrollment number), read from right to left, starting at the rightmost digit.
- Task: perform histogram equalization and give the resulting image Y.
- Worked example: matrícula 0123456789 gives X = [9 8 7; 6 5 4; 3 2 1].
- **Topics:** histogram computation, PDF/CDF, the discrete equalization transform s_k = round((L−1)·CDF(r_k)), and rebuilding the image.
- **Skill:** pure computation by hand. The pixel values depend on the student's own matrícula, so repeated digits matter.

## QD2 (p. 6, discursive)
- Image (5×5, 8-bit): X has only three nonzero pixels. X(2,4) = 7, X(3,3) = 3 and X(4,2) = 4. They lie on an anti-diagonal. All other entries are 0.
- Mask: h = [c b c; b a b; c b c], where a, b, c are the last three digits of the matrícula. a is the third from the right, b the second and c the last. Any digit equal to 0 must be replaced by 1.
- Task: compute Y = X * h as a 5×5 matrix.
- Example 1: matrícula 0123456789 gives h = [9 8 9; 8 7 8; 9 8 9].
- Example 2: matrícula 9876543210 gives a = 2, b = 1, c = 0→1, so h = [1 1 1; 1 2 1; 1 1 1].
- **Topics:** 2D discrete convolution, zero padding and a same-size 5×5 output, and the linearity/impulse-response view.
- **Skill:** computation by hand.
- **Shortcut:** h is symmetric, so there is no flip issue. Y is the sum of three copies of h centered on the three impulses and scaled by 7, 3 and 4. Overlapping regions add, and anything outside the 5×5 frame is cropped.

## Overall topic map
- **Frequency domain / DCT:** QO1, QO2.
- **Spatial filtering, sharpening, edges:** QO2, QO5, QD2.
- **Color models (RGB, HSI, safe colors):** QO3, QO6, QO7, QO8.
- **Noise, histograms and restoration filters:** QO4.
- **Histogram equalization:** QD1.
- **Conceptual only:** QO1–QO5.
- **Short calculations:** QO6–QO8.
- **Full hand computations:** QD1, QD2.

Pages consulted: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6
